sheet-1-1.description: The main part of Sheet 1 covers the centre of New Gretna, a village of about 600 people in Bass River Township in south-eastern Burlington County. New York Road, the paved through road (today US 9), runs up the sheet from the south-west corner, and Allentown Road or Maple Avenue crosses the sheet from its junction with New York Road at the lower right towards Rotan at the left; the short street continuing east of the junction is drawn but not named. North is towards the left of the sheet. Canby leaves New York Road eastward near the top right, and Rotan runs off Maple Avenue at the left; a dashed Private Road crosses the lower part of the sheet, with a lane running south from it. The blocks hold scattered frame dwellings with stables, sheds, chicken coops and auto houses on deep lots. Along Maple Avenue stand the First Presbyterian Church, the Public School and the Community Hall; New Gretna Hotel faces New York Road at the junction, a K. of P. Hall stands on its east side, and M. A. Cramer's garage with gasoline tanks and an auto repair shop sit near the bottom of the sheet. A water tower on a wood tower stands in the block west of New York Road. The sheet carries the title cartouche (population 600, prevailing winds west and north-west), a locator map of New Jersey, the key to symbols, the scale bar and a note that the town has no water facilities and no fire department, that New York Road is paved and other roads are sandy gravel, the ground level and lighting electric. The upper left corner, cut off by a heavy line, is an inset continuing Maple Avenue westward (part 2). Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: New York Road is US 9 today; OpenStreetMap carries it without a name (ref US 9 only), so it was added to the reference extract under the name 'US 9'.
Allentown Road or Maple Avenue is North Maple Avenue (CR 679) west of New York Road; the unnamed street east of the junction is South Maple Ave.
Rotan and Canby are marked 'Arbitrary' on the sheet (names given by the map-maker); Rotan is Riverside Drive today and Canby is Bower Lane.
The dashed Private Road follows the line of today's Frenchs Lane and its parcel boundaries; the modern roadway runs off the drawn line, so it was not used for control.

Sheet 1, 100 ft. Centre of New Gretna: New York Road (US 9) with Allentown Road or Maple Avenue (North Maple Avenue), Rotan (Riverside Drive), Canby (Bower Lane), Private Road (Frenchs Lane line). Two parts: 1 main, 2 inset top left continuing Maple Avenue west of Rotan with Kelso (Adams Avenue). Carries the title cartouche, locator map and key (left in the mask, inside block 17). North to the left.

sheet-1-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 1 is an inset in the upper left corner of the sheet, set off by a heavy line, that continues Allentown Road or Maple Avenue westward beyond Rotan, at the north-western edge of New Gretna in Bass River Township. It is drawn at the same scale (100 feet to an inch) and orientation as the main part, with north towards the left, and adjoins it along Rotan. Maple Avenue runs across the lower part of the inset; Kelso, a 20 ft street, and Rotan, 30 ft, run off it towards the top of the sheet, which is east. The blocks, numbered 15, 16 and 20 on the sheet, hold a few frame dwellings with sheds, a store-house and small outbuildings along Maple Avenue, and much open land behind them; a building stands at the Rotan corner. The top edge of the inset is marked 'No exposure'. A compass rose sits on the dividing line below the inset.
notes: Kelso and Rotan are marked 'Arbitrary' on the sheet; Kelso matches Adams Avenue and Rotan Riverside Drive today.
Placed from Maple Avenue / Riverside Drive alone, at the scale and rotation of part 1; Adams Avenue's modern junction falls about 4 m from where the inset draws Kelso, so it was left out.

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of Sheet 2 continues New York Road (today US 9) south-west from the foot of Sheet 1 through the southern half of New Gretna, in Bass River Township, Burlington County. North is towards the left; New York Road runs straight down the right-hand side of the sheet to the fork where Philadelphia Road (today CR 542) branches off at the bottom. Mace's Landing Road leaves New York Road eastward in the lower right quarter. Lots on both sides of New York Road carry frame dwellings with stables, auto houses and sheds; St. Paul's M.E. Church and the Post Office stand on the east side, and a garage with gasoline tanks stands at the fork. The top of the sheet repeats M. A. Cramer's garage from Sheet 1. The large area to the left of New York Road (block 20) is almost empty apart from a few outbuildings and a poultry house; a compass rose and the title oval 'June 1930 New Gretna N.J.' are printed on the sheet. The lower left corner, cut off by a heavy line, is an inset continuing Philadelphia Road and Old New York Road (part 2). Drawn at 100 feet to an inch, but the fitted scale is about 3.5 percent larger than Sheet 1's.
notes: Mace's Landing Road is Amasas Landing Road today.
Philadelphia Road is CR 542 (Hammonton Road beyond the Old New York Road Spur); the modern fork with US 9 has been rebuilt about 40 m from the drawn one and was not used.
Placed from two points carried from Sheet 1 at the Cramer garage and the Mace's Landing Road junction, as a similarity transform (helmert).

Two parts: 1 main, 2 inset lower left continuing Philadelphia Road and Old New York Road (Old New York Road Spur) beyond the fork. Drawn about 3.5 percent larger than nominal relative to Sheet 1. North to the left.

sheet-2-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 2 is an inset in the lower left corner of the sheet, set off by a heavy line, continuing the roads south-west of the fork shown at the bottom of part 1, at the south-western edge of New Gretna. It is drawn at the same orientation as the rest of the sheet, with north to the upper left (an arrow marks it). Philadelphia Road, 40 ft wide, runs up the inset; Old New York Road (33 ft) leaves it towards the lower right, joined near the junction by a curved cut-off, and the 60 ft New York Road sweeps across the top of the inset in a long curve. A Private Road (20 ft) leaves Philadelphia Road westward opposite Old New York Road, and another Private Road (24 ft) runs south from Old New York Road near the dividing line. Frame dwellings with chicken coops, auto houses, a spring house and other outbuildings line Philadelphia Road and Old New York Road; the blocks are numbered 20, 22, 23 and 24. The edges are marked 'No exposure'. Drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Philadelphia Road is CR 542 / Hammonton Road, Old New York Road is Old New York Road Spur, the curved New York Road is US 9.
The Private Road west of Philadelphia Road matches the West Road track; the Private Road south of Old New York Road lies near Hillside Avenue, whose modern junction is about 18 m from the drawn one.
Placed from the Philadelphia Road / Old New York Road junction alone, at the scale and rotation of part 1 (helmert with a derived point).
